title: 26th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The 26th sitting of the third session opened on 27 November 2025 at 09:01 with 33 members reported present, 4 on leave and none on official travel. Two bills were formally introduced (first reading), and members then held opening debates on a bill on road (land) transport, an amendment to the Tourism Act, a resolution about how courts treat people differently, and an amendment to the Fiscal Responsibility Act. The road transport and tourism debates were closed, with a vote promised for later in the day; the court resolution was still being debated when the sitting paused for a break from 10:30 to 11:00, and the fiscal bill debate was under way when this part ends. No votes were taken in this part; the text has some garbled digits and wording. This part covers the rest of the debate on the State Fiscal Responsibility bill, a long debate on the government bill to trim benefits for former Presidents and set benefits for former Vice Presidents, and committee reports on two decentralisation and local-election bills. After the midday break the House passed one amendment to the decentralisation bill, then passed both of those bills, and also voted to accept four new bills for committee study. Several figures in the speeches are garbled in the text layer and are not repeated here.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: On the transport bill: supported it, said it should be enforced equally on MPs and officials, and urged parking buildings in Male' soon.
On the court resolution: opposed it and argued the courts were put under political pressure during the earlier MDP government, so the resolution should not be tabled.
Responded to a point of order and to the Speaker's reminder to respect the rules, and repeated his criticism of MDP-era events involving judges.
Supported the former Presidents amendment and wanted the committee to reduce costs further, including cuts to MPs' own pay and benefits.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: On the court resolution: opposed it, pointing to the MDP's record on the judiciary and saying courts are now independent.
On the fiscal bill: supported it, saying the extra time helps build strong, workable regulations.
Backed the former Presidents amendment as a way to cut state spending, saying it should apply to former leaders and MPs alike.
Presented the temporary committee's report on the Decentralisation bill and later the report on the Local Councils Elections bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Backed the bill and said everyone, including MPs, must follow parking and traffic rules.
Said the government is changing many laws and expressed support for the President and the government.
Supported the former Presidents amendment, describing the office running allowance for former Presidents and arguing benefits should reflect service to the nation.
Said the all-party committee drew on public input; described the women's seat share and council changes and the savings he expects.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Presented the resolution, citing short detention orders in some cases and long ones in others as signs courts treat people unequally.
Raised a point of order that calling for people to be killed is a serious offence under the law.
On the fiscal bill: opposed it, saying it reverses amendments the PNC itself introduced and that the 2026 budget was prepared against the law.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: On the transport bill: supported it but said results depend on enforcement, funding and avoiding corruption, and asked that a carrying capacity for vehicles be set.
On the court resolution: said people have lost trust in the courts, pointing to unequal treatment of detainees and years-long delays at the High Court.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: On the tourism bill: supported it, saying it opens opportunities for Maldivian companies and youth and protects investors with longer deadlines.
On the court resolution: said people have long felt courts lack fairness, but that protests should stay peaceful and lawful, and said the government is working on court cases.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Opposed the Fiscal Responsibility amendment, saying repeated deadline extensions show the government is not delivering what earlier laws require.
On the local council bills, said he could not back the cuts and questioned how the 40 percent women's share would work.
Argued that fewer elected council seats hurts youth jobs while political appointments stay high, and that appointment powers need limits too.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shamin Habeeb
positions: Presented the Road Transport Bill as a modern legal framework covering vehicle registration, licences, public transport, enforcement and penalties across nine chapters.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Supported the bill, hoping it ends the problem of cars needing a garage slot to register.
Said parking buildings near the Mahchangolhi roads would clear narrow streets and help ambulances.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Supported the bill but raised concern about Article 66, which allows a licence to be suspended for breaking any law, using taxi drivers as an example.
Asked that regulations stay within limits set by the law and said many issues can be fixed at committee stage.

speakers.name: Mohamed Sinan
positions: Presented the Tourism Act amendment: lets state companies lease sites for resorts and tourism training resorts, extends development deadlines, defines lagoon areas and licenses tour operators.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the tourism amendment and said it clears up confusion for investors about lagoon areas, training resorts and licensing.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the tourism amendment as favouring Maldivian companies and youth jobs, noting most tourism investment in the industry comes from abroad.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Presented the fiscal bill: the first fiscal responsibility charter must be published within 24 months, and the time for making regulations goes from 6 to 24 months.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Presented the government bill to review certain benefits for former Presidents and to set benefits for former Vice Presidents, amending several articles of the 2009 law.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Supported amending the 2009 law but asked the committee to look at double pensions and at MPs' benefits after leaving office.
Said the state should deal with its largest burdens first rather than only small items.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Opposed the council report, saying cutting elected representatives is not a good-faith step and he could not accept the population-based council numbers.
Questioned why Malé City keeps many councillors and a mayor while small islands lose seats, and noted the abolished atoll councils' youth programmes.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Moved an amendment to article 47 of the Decentralisation bill, adding a clause letting the government proceed with its development projects if councils do not grant needed permits in reasonable time.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Seconded the Funadhoo amendment to the Decentralisation bill.

decisions: Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir replaces Maradhoo member Ahmed Didi on the Economic Committee (MDP nominee).
The Fiscal Responsibility Act amendment bill and the former-Presidents law (Law 2009/9) amendment bill were read for the first time.
Debate on the Road Transport Bill and the Tourism Act amendment bill was closed, with each to be put to a vote at the day's voting time.
The sitting paused from 10:30 to 11:00; the Speaker said remaining debate on the court resolution would wait for a later day.
Debate on the State Fiscal Responsibility amendment bill was closed and the bill was later accepted 55-10 and sent to the Finance Committee.
Debate on the former Presidents bill was closed after no more members asked to speak; the bill was accepted 64-0 and sent to the Finance Committee.
The Land Transport bill was accepted 65-0 and sent to the National Development and Heritage Committee.
The Tourism law (No. 2/99) amendment bill was accepted 53-11 and sent to the Economic Committee.
The Funadhoo amendment to the Decentralisation bill passed 56-3 with 3 abstentions.
The Decentralisation (No. 2010/7) amendment bill passed 54-11 with the House's amendments.
The Local Councils Elections (No. 2010/10) amendment bill passed 55-10.
The next sitting was set for Monday 1 December 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept the Land Transport bill for committee study (Kurendhoo, government)
Accept the bill amending the Tourism law No. 2/99 (North Hithadhoo, government)
Accept the bill amending the State Fiscal Responsibility law No. 2024/30 (Huraa, government)
Accept the bill amending the former Presidents benefits law No. 2009/9 (Hulhudhoo, government)
Funadhoo amendment to the Decentralisation bill (article 107-3(n) on permits for government projects)
Pass the bill amending the Decentralisation law No. 2010/7, with the House's amendments
Pass the bill amending the Local Councils Elections law No. 2010/10 (third reading)
